# Independent audits: moment-body inball and affine-width hinge

## Quantitative moment-body inball

`candidate cf94bd7190201a57` passes in full.
The homothetic body (1-theta)p+theta K lies in K and has exactly the
prescribed mass. Mixing a mass-T balanced source and a mass-s central
source with coefficients (t-s)/(T-s) and (T-t)/(T-s) preserves source
domination even when the two source measures overlap. Their total
mass is exactly t and their common integer centroid remains j. The
displayed homothetic coefficient and inradius follow. The suggested
t=D_j/2 and s=min(D_j/4,w_j/2) satisfy every strict inequality.

## Affine-width-normalized hinge

`candidate d233b11c4a70933f` also passes
in full. Checked explicitly:

* The transformed integer normal and offset reproduce the original
  margin under every stated lattice-preserving affine fiber shear.
  Both D_int and D_all transform by the continuous linear part A;
  the determinant multiplies all relevant masses and hinge integrals.
* The quotient-gradient term is exactly -Psi_i R_i, with R_i an
  exposed point of D and u_i.R_i=1. The section moments retain the
  factor 1/|u_i| and the same trace density in every component.
* The contact equations and same-real-base centroid comparison give
  alpha_0 Psi_i<=alpha_0 c_i+r_i S_i. The active budget multiplier
  term cannot be omitted, and the abnormal objective case remains
  explicitly possible.
* For an arbitrary simplex, R_i=vertex_i-opposite_facet_centroid is
  an actual supporting difference of K-K. Its canonical cap-centroid
  displacement is d R_i/(d+1)^2=Psi_i R_i/c_i. This proves the stated
  normalized joint stress without regular-simplex assumptions.
* For the binary square-height example, the allowed mixing weight
  at vertex(1,1) is exactly [max(0,s+t-1),min(s,t)], giving the real
  fiber width and W=1+L/2. Both exact hinge minima, all-halfspace
  sharp depth, and the D_all degeneration follow with the stated
  constants.

No correction or unresolved technical qualification was found.
